transform.name: PRIVATE_FORCED_FALSE_LITERAL_PADDING
transform.definition: For every clause C_i of F introduce a private fresh variable y_i and replace C_i by the pair (C_i OR y_i) and (not y_i).
transform.semantic_status: Exactly equivalent after eliminating y_i; the unit clause forces y_i=0, restoring C_i.

theorem.statement: delta*(T(F)) = delta*(F) for every CNF F.
proof: Take any clause subset Q of T(F). For each original index i classify Q as containing neither transformed clause, only padded clause, only unit clause, or both.
Let B be indices where both clauses are present, P padded-only indices, U unit-only indices.
The number of selected clauses is 2|B|+|P|+|U|.
The selected private variables are exactly |B|+|P|+|U|, while original variables appearing are Var(B union P).
For the reverse inequality choose an original sub-clause-set B attaining delta*(F) and in T(F) select both transformed clauses for every i in B. Its deficiency is exactly |B|-|Var(B)|=delta*(F).

R44BD_effect.selector_application: Applying private forced padding to the R44BE disjoint-copy selector merge leaves its maximum deficiency exactly a+b-1.
R44BD_effect.consequence: The additive selector debt cannot be repaired by attaching one private forced Boolean variable to each clause, even though those variables appear to add matching capacity.
